claim: Transposable elements (TEs) are mobile genetic elements that make up a large fraction of mammalian genomes.
source: Transposable elements (TEs) are mobile genetic elements that make up a large fraction of mammalian genomes.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in genomics supported by extensive research.

claim: The majority of TEs are epigenetically silenced by DNA methylation in somatic cells.
source: While select TEs have been co-opted in host genomes to have function, the majority of these elements are epigenetically silenced by DNA methylation in somatic cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of epigenetics.

claim: Some TEs in mice, including the Intracisternal A-particle (IAP) subfamily of retrotransposons, display interindividual variation in DNA methylation.
source: However, some TEs in mice, including the Intracisternal A-particle (IAP) subfamily of retrotransposons, have been shown to display interindividual variation in DNA methylation.
evidence: This statement references existing research findings.

claim: IAP sequence differences and strain-specific KRAB zinc finger proteins (KZFPs) may influence the methylation state of IAPs.
source: Recent work has revealed that IAP sequence differences and strain-specific KRAB zinc finger proteins (KZFPs) may influence the methylation state of these IAPs.
evidence: This is based on recent research findings in the field.

claim: Sequence content and genomic context influence the likelihood that IAPs become variably methylated.
source: Here, we report that sequence content and genomic context influence the likelihood that IAPs become variably methylated.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript supported by experimental data.

claim: IAPs that differ from consensus IAP sequences have altered KZFP recruitment.
source: IAPs that differ from consensus IAP sequences have altered KZFP recruitment that can lead to decreased KAP1 recruitment when in proximity of constitutively expressed genes.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IAPs with altered KZFP recruitment can lead to decreased KAP1 recruitment when in proximity of constitutively expressed genes.
source: IAPs that differ from consensus IAP sequences have altered KZFP recruitment that can lead to decreased KAP1 recruitment when in proximity of constitutively expressed genes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing KAP1 binding patterns.

claim: Variably methylated IAPs have a high CpG density, similar to CpG islands.
source: These variably methylated loci have a high CpG density, similar to CpG islands, and can be bound by ZF-CxxC proteins, providing a potential mechanism to maintain this permissive chromatin environment and protect from DNA methylation.
evidence: This is supported by CpG density analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Variably methylated IAPs can be bound by ZF-CxxC proteins.
source: These variably methylated loci have a high CpG density, similar to CpG islands, and can be bound by ZF-CxxC proteins, providing a potential mechanism to maintain this permissive chromatin environment and protect from DNA methylation.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq and CUT&RUN data for CFP1 and TET1.

claim: ZF-CxxC protein binding provides a potential mechanism to maintain a permissive chromatin environment and protect from DNA methylation.
source: These variably methylated loci have a high CpG density, similar to CpG islands, and can be bound by ZF-CxxC proteins, providing a potential mechanism to maintain this permissive chromatin environment and protect from DNA methylation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the data and known functions of ZF-CxxC proteins.

claim: Variably methylated IAPs escape silencing through both attenuation of KZFP binding and recognition by ZF-CxxC proteins to maintain a hypomethylated state.
source: These observations indicate that variably methylated IAPs escape silencing through both attenuation of KZFP binding and recognition by ZF-CxxC proteins to maintain a hypomethylated state.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript based on multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Certain TEs can escape silencing and behave as sites of interindividual epigenetic variability.
source: Certain TEs, however, can escape silencing and behave as sites of interindividual epigenetic variability (Bakshi et al., 2016; Dolinoy et al., 2007a; Gunasekara et al., 2019; Hernando-Herraez et al., 2015; Oey et al., 2015; Reiss et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Variably methylated loci have been reported to be sensitive to environmental stimuli such as diet and exposure to toxins.
source: These loci have been reported to be sensitive to environmental stimuli such as diet and exposure to toxins (Dolinoy et al., 2007b; Morgan et al., 1999; Rosenfeld et al., 2013; Waterland et al., 2007; Waterland and Jirtle, 2003), although this field remains an area of active research (Bertozzi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Agouti viable yellow mouse is the most well-studied metastable epiallele.
source: The well-most studied metastable epiallele is present in the Agouti viable yellow mouse, where genetically identical mice display phenotypic diversity that manifests as a range of coat colors and susceptibility to obesity (Bernal et al., 2011; Rakyan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citations.

claim: Genetically identical Agouti viable yellow mice display phenotypic diversity that manifests as a range of coat colors and susceptibility to obesity.
source: The well-most studied metastable epiallele is present in the Agouti viable yellow mouse, where genetically identical mice display phenotypic diversity that manifests as a range of coat colors and susceptibility to obesity (Bernal et al., 2011; Rakyan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Variable coat color in Agouti viable yellow mice has been linked to the methylation state of a novel insertion of an Intracisternal A-particle (IAP) retrotransposon.
source: This variable coat color has been linked to the methylation state of a novel insertion of an Intracisternal A-particle (IAP) retrotransposon (Dolinoy et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Variable methylation of the IAP in Agouti mice contributes to variable transcription of the agouti gene across all tissues and variation in coat color, hyperphagia and hyperinsulinemia.
source: Variable methylation of this IAP contributes to variable transcription of the agouti gene across all tissues and variation in coat color, hyperphagia and hyperinsulinemia (Bernal et al., 2011; Rakyan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Roughly 50 loci are variably methylated in mice in a manner similar to the IAP that drives the agouti mouse phenotype.
source: Recent work profiling interindividual epigenetic variability in mice identified roughly 50 loci that are variably methylated in a manner similar to the IAP that drives the agouti mouse phenotype (Adams et al., 2012; Bertozzi et al., 2020; Elmer et al., 2020; Kazachenka et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: The majority of variably methylated loci are IAP retrotransposons (VM-IAPs).
source: The majority of these variably methylated loci are IAP retrotransposons (VM-IAPs) (Bertozzi et al., 2020; Faulk et al., 2013; Kazachenka et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: IAPs are silenced in a sequence-specific manner by KRAB-domain containing zinc finger proteins (KZFPs).
source: IAPs are silenced in a sequence-specific manner by KRAB-domain containing zinc finger proteins (KZFPs) (Coluccio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: KZFPs recruit KAP1, which in turn recruits repressive protein complexes to deposit H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at IAP loci.
source: KZFPs recruit KAP1, also known as TRIM28, which, in turn, recruits repressive protein complexes to deposit H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at these loci (Bulut-Karslioglu et al., 2014; Ecco et al., 2017; Ecco et al., 2016; Schultz et al., 2002; Turelli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: KZFPs and KAP1 regulate TEs in somatic cells as well as embryonic stem cells.
source: While this has been thought to happen primarily in embryonic stem cells, recent work has demonstrated that KZFPs and KAP1 regulated TEs in somatic cells as well (Ecco et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent research.

claim: KZFPs have evolved in clusters through imperfect gene duplication and spontaneous mutations that can allow for the recognition of novel TEs.
source: KZFPs have evolved in clusters through imperfect gene duplication and spontaneous mutations that can allow for the recognition of novel TEs (Imbeault et al., 2017; Kauzlaric et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: TEs can mutate and escape from KZFP targeted silencing over time.
source: Over time, TEs can mutate and escape from KZFP targeted silencing (Imbeault et al., 2017; Kauzlaric et al., 2017; Wolf et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: KZFPs are engaged in an evolutionary arms race with TEs to maintain their silencing.
source: It has been proposed that these KZFPs are engaged in an evolutionary arms race with TEs to maintain their silencing (Jacobs et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed in previous research.

claim: IAPs have an unusually high CpG content that is more similar to CpG islands (CGIs) than to the rest of the mouse genome.
source: IAPs have an unusually high CpG content that is more similar to CpG islands (CGIs) than to the rest of the mouse genome (Elmer et al., 2020; Kazachenka et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CGIs are generally hypomethylated and can recruit ZF-CxxC proteins, which help maintain a permissive chromatin environment.
source: CGIs are generally hypomethylated and can recruit ZF-CxxC proteins, which help maintain a permissive chromatin environment (Clouaire et al., 2012; Gu et al., 2018; Mikkelsen et al., 2007; Thomson et al., 2010; van de Lagemaat et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: CFP1 is a subunit of the SET1 complex that deposits H3K4me3.
source: Notable CxxC domain containing proteins include CFP1, which is a subunit of the SET1 complex that deposit H3K4me3, and TET1/TET3, which are responsible for the active removal of methylation from CpG dinucleotides to maintain a hypomethylated state (Gu et al., 2018; Tahiliani et al., 2009; Williams et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TET1/TET3 are responsible for the active removal of methylation from CpG dinucleotides to maintain a hypomethylated state.
source: Notable CxxC domain containing proteins include CFP1, which is a subunit of the SET1 complex that deposit H3K4me3, and TET1/TET3, which are responsible for the active removal of methylation from CpG dinucleotides to maintain a hypomethylated state (Gu et al., 2018; Tahiliani et al., 2009; Williams et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mammalian genomes have an underrepresentation of CpG dinucleotides as a result of deamination at methylated cytosines over evolutionary time.
source: Mammalian genomes in general have an underrepresentation of CpG dinucleotides as a result of deamination at methylated cytosines over evolutionary time (Duncan and Miller, 1980; Crayle et al., 2016; Shen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The CpG richness of IAPs is potentially due to the fact these elements are more recent additions to the genome that have yet to undergo evolutionary deamination at methylated CpG dinucleotides.
source: The 'richness' of CpG dinucleotides at IAPs is potentially due to the fact these elements are more recent additions to the genome that have yet to undergo 'evolutionary' deamination at methylated CpG dinucleotides.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on evolutionary principles.

claim: Recently evolved CpG dense TEs have the potential to be hypomethylated when there is no targeted suppression of these elements.
source: It has been previously shown that recently evolved CpG dense TEs have the potential to be hypomethylated when there is no targeted suppression of these elements (Jacobs et al., 2014; Long et al., 2016; Ward et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Multiple sequence alignment and hierarchical clustering identified four sequence 'clades' for IAPLTR1s.
source: This profiling resulted in the characterization of four sequence 'clades' for IAPLTR1s (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2 and Supplementary file 1), two sequence 'clades' for the IAPLTR2s (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1), and three sequence clades for IAPEz-ints.
evidence: This is a result from the sequence analysis performed in the study.

claim: Multiple sequence alignment and hierarchical clustering identified two sequence 'clades' for IAPLTR2s.
source: This profiling resulted in the characterization of four sequence 'clades' for IAPLTR1s (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2 and Supplementary file 1), two sequence 'clades' for the IAPLTR2s (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1), and three sequence clades for IAPEz-ints.
evidence: This is a result from the sequence analysis performed in the study.

claim: Multiple sequence alignment and hierarchical clustering identified three sequence clades for IAPEz-ints.
source: This profiling resulted in the characterization of four sequence 'clades' for IAPLTR1s (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2 and Supplementary file 1), two sequence 'clades' for the IAPLTR2s (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1), and three sequence clades for IAPEz-ints.
evidence: This is a result from the sequence analysis performed in the study.

claim: Clade 1 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP989 and Gm21082.
source: We identified that clade 1 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP989 and Gm21082, while clade 2 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP429 (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clade 2 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP429.
source: We identified that clade 1 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP989 and Gm21082, while clade 2 IAPLTR1 elements have evidence of binding by ZFP429 (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clade 3 and clade 4 IAPLTR1 elements do not show evidence of binding by ZFP989, Gm21082, or ZFP429 and have decreased KAP1 binding.
source: However, clade 3 and clade 4 IAPLTR1 elements do not show evidence of binding by these KZFPs and have decreased KAP1 binding (Figure 1A and B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clade 1 IAPLTR2s are bound by ZFP429.
source: Similar analysis with IAPLTR2s demonstrated that clade 1 IAPLTR2s are bound by ZFP429, while clade 2 IAPLTR2 elements are largely bound by ZFP989 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clade 2 IAPLTR2 elements are largely bound by ZFP989.
source: Similar analysis with IAPLTR2s demonstrated that clade 1 IAPLTR2s are bound by ZFP429, while clade 2 IAPLTR2 elements are largely bound by ZFP989 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both IAPLTR2 clades have evidence of KAP1 binding.
source: Both clades have evidence of KAP1 binding (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: IAPEz-int clade γ elements displayed the weakest Gm14419 binding and the lowest KAP1 signal compared to clades α and β.
source: When profiling KZFP and KAP1 occupation at the IAPEz-int variants, we observed that clade γ elements displayed the weakest Gm14419 binding and the lowest KAP1 signal compared to clades α and β (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: VM-IAPLTR1s were significantly enriched at IAPs with IAPLTR1 clade three elements flanking IAPEz-int clade γ elements.
source: We observed that VM-IAPLTR1s were significantly enriched at IAPs with IAPLTR1 clade three elements flanking IAPEz-int clade γ elements (Figure 1C), and VM-IAPLTR2 elements were significantly enriched at solo IAPLTR2 clade 1 elements (P-value < 1e-16 as determined using a Fisher exact test) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: VM-IAPLTR2 elements were significantly enriched at solo IAPLTR2 clade 1 elements (P-value < 1e-16).
source: We observed that VM-IAPLTR1s were significantly enriched at IAPs with IAPLTR1 clade three elements flanking IAPEz-int clade γ elements (Figure 1C), and VM-IAPLTR2 elements were significantly enriched at solo IAPLTR2 clade 1 elements (P-value < 1e-16 as determined using a Fisher exact test) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: 83% of VM-IAPLTR1s were within 50 kb of a constitutively expressed gene.
source: We found that 83 % of the VM-IAPLTR1s were within 50 kb of a constitutively expressed gene, while the remaining 17 % of VM-IAPLTR1s were less than 1 kb from an annotated enhancer element.
evidence: This is based on genomic location analysis of VM-IAPs.

claim: 17% of VM-IAPLTR1s were less than 1 kb from an annotated enhancer element.
source: We found that 83 % of the VM-IAPLTR1s were within 50 kb of a constitutively expressed gene, while the remaining 17 % of VM-IAPLTR1s were less than 1 kb from an annotated enhancer element.
evidence: This is based on genomic location analysis of VM-IAPs.

claim: Only 12% of non-VM IAPs were proximal to a constitutively expressed gene.
source: In contrast, only 12 % of the non-VM IAPs were proximal to a constitutively expressed gene and 7 % were proximal to an enhancer (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on genomic location analysis of non-VM IAPs.

claim: 7% of non-VM IAPs were proximal to an enhancer.
source: In contrast, only 12 % of the non-VM IAPs were proximal to a constitutively expressed gene and 7 % were proximal to an enhancer (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on genomic location analysis of non-VM IAPs.

claim: Clade 3-4 IAPLTR1s are more polymorphic across mouse strains than the other clades.
source: We found that clade 3–4 IAPLTR1s, which have the lowest KAP1 binding of the IAPLTR1 clades and IAPEz-int clade γ elements are more polymorphic across mouse strains than the other clades (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is based on analysis of structural variants between mouse strains.

claim: IAPEz-int clade γ elements are more polymorphic across mouse strains than the other clades.
source: We found that clade 3–4 IAPLTR1s, which have the lowest KAP1 binding of the IAPLTR1 clades and IAPEz-int clade γ elements are more polymorphic across mouse strains than the other clades (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is based on analysis of structural variants between mouse strains.

claim: IAPLTR2 clade 1 elements are more likely to be polymorphic across mouse strains.
source: Additionally, we found that IAPLTR2 clade 1 elements, which are more prone to be variably methylated, are more likely to be polymorphic across mouse strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is based on analysis of structural variants between mouse strains.

claim: TE subfamilies with a higher average CpG density had a larger percentage of elements that are variably methylated.
source: We observed that TE subfamilies with a higher average CpG density had a larger percentage of elements that are variably methylated, with IAPLTRs being the most CpG dense and having the largest percentage of variably methylated elements (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of CpG density and variable methylation across TE subfamilies.

claim: IAPLTRs are the most CpG dense TEs and have the largest percentage of variably methylated elements.
source: We observed that TE subfamilies with a higher average CpG density had a larger percentage of elements that are variably methylated, with IAPLTRs being the most CpG dense and having the largest percentage of variably methylated elements (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of CpG density and variable methylation across TE subfamilies.

claim: The CpG content of VM-IAPLTR1s and VM-IAPLTR2s is similar to non-VM-IAPLTR1s and non-VM-IAPLTR2s.
source: The CpG content of VM-IAPLTR1s and VM-IAPLTR2s is similar to non-VM-IAPLTR1s and VM-IAPLTR2s, indicating that high CpG content alone is not sufficient to induce variable methylation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on CpG density analysis comparing VM and non-VM IAPs.

claim: High CpG content alone is not sufficient to induce variable methylation.
source: The CpG content of VM-IAPLTR1s and VM-IAPLTR2s is similar to non-VM-IAPLTR1s and VM-IAPLTR2s, indicating that high CpG content alone is not sufficient to induce variable methylation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CpG density data.

claim: TET1 binding is increased at clade 3 IAPLTR1s elements.
source: Utilizing a publicly available ChIP-seq dataset for the ZF-CxxC-domain containing protein TET1 in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) (Gu et al., 2018), we identified increased TET1 binding at clade3 IAPLTR1s elements, which contains the most variably methylated elements (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published TET1 ChIP-seq data.

claim: VM-IAPs displayed a significant increase in CpG methylation in Tet1 KO cells.
source: We furthermore profiled CpG methylation of VM-IAPLTRs in Tet1 knockout (KO) and Tet1/Dnmt3a double knockout (DKO) mESCs (Gu et al., 2018) and found that VM-IAPs displayed a significant increase in CpG methylation in the Tet1 KO cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published methylation data from Tet1 KO cells.

claim: The increase in methylation at VM-IAPs in Tet1 KO cells is reversed when both Dnmt3a and Tet1 are knocked out in mESCs.
source: This increase in methylation is reversed when both Dnmt3a and Tet1 are knocked out in mESCs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published methylation data from Tet1/Dnmt3a DKO cells.

claim: CFP1 binding appears to be specific to VM-IAPLTRs.
source: We also profiled the recruitment of another ZF-CxxC protein, CFP1, using existing CFP1 ChIP-seq data from C57Bl/6 mice and observed CFP1 binding appears to be specific to VM-IAPLTRs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published CFP1 ChIP-seq data.

claim: VM-IAPs were more likely to be enriched for H3K4me3 compared to non-variable IAPs.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Bertozzi et al., 2020), we observed that VM-IAPs were more likely to ben enriched for H3K4me3 compared to non-variable IAPs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published H3K4me3 ChIP-seq data.

claim: Evolutionarily recent TEs were overrepresented in the variably methylated dataset in humans.
source: We observed that evolutionarily recent TEs were overrepresented in the variably methylated dataset (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of human variably methylated loci.

claim: TE subfamilies with a higher CpG density are more likely to be variably methylated in humans.
source: We also found the TE subfamilies with a higher CpG density are more likely to be variably methylated (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), with the highly CpG dense transposable element subfamily LTR12C having both one of the highest CpG densities and one of highest percentage of elements that are variably methylated.
evidence: This is based on analysis of human variably methylated loci and CpG density.

claim: LTR12C has one of the highest CpG densities and one of highest percentage of elements that are variably methylated in humans.
source: We also found the TE subfamilies with a higher CpG density are more likely to be variably methylated (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), with the highly CpG dense transposable element subfamily LTR12C having both one of the highest CpG densities and one of highest percentage of elements that are variably methylated.
evidence: This is based on analysis of human variably methylated loci and CpG density.

claim: LTR12Cs are recently evolved TEs that have previously been shown to have latent regulatory potential.
source: LTR12Cs are recently evolved TEs that have previously been shown to have latent regulatory potential (Ward et al., 2013) and can act as cryptic promoter elements in cancer cells (Babaian and Mager, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: LTR12Cs can act as cryptic promoter elements in cancer cells.
source: LTR12Cs are recently evolved TEs that have previously been shown to have latent regulatory potential (Ward et al., 2013) and can act as cryptic promoter elements in cancer cells (Babaian and Mager, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: TE-derived CGIs were hypomethylated in Tc1 mouse liver in the absence of KZFP-mediated silencing.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Jacobs et al., 2014; Long et al., 2016; Ward et al., 2013), we found that TE-derived CGIs were hypomethylated in the absence of KZFP-mediated silencing (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on MinION nanopore sequencing data from Tc1 mouse liver.

claim: TE-derived CGIs that can be targeted by KZFPs shared between mice and humans were largely methylated in Tc1 mouse liver.
source: In contrast, TE-derived CGIs that can be targeted by KZFPs shared between mice and humans were largely methylated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on MinION nanopore sequencing data from Tc1 mouse liver.

claim: CpG dense TEs that are not targeted by KZFPs displayed CFP1 recruitment in Tc1 mouse liver.
source: We observed that CpG dense TEs that are not targeted by KZFPs displayed CFP1 recruitment, while the methylated CpG poor TEs have no CFP1 signal (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on CFP1 CUT&RUN data from Tc1 mouse liver.

claim: Methylated CpG poor TEs have no CFP1 signal in Tc1 mouse liver.
source: We observed that CpG dense TEs that are not targeted by KZFPs displayed CFP1 recruitment, while the methylated CpG poor TEs have no CFP1 signal (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on CFP1 CUT&RUN data from Tc1 mouse liver.

claim: CFP1 binding at CpG dense TEs on human chromosome 21 was unique to Tc1 mice and not present in humans.
source: This CFP1 binding was also unique to the Tc1 mice as there was no CFP1 binding at these loci in humans (Figure 4C), while non-TE CGIs in both the mouse and human genomes have CFP1 binding (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of CFP1 data from Tc1 mice and humans.

claim: In the absence of targeted KZFP-mediated silencing, TEs with high CpG content can be hypomethylated and bound by ZF-CxxC proteins.
source: Together this work demonstrates that in the absence of targeted KZFP-mediated silencing, TEs with high CpG content can be hypomethylated and bound by ZF-CxxC proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Tc1 mouse experiments.

claim: 69 loci had novel H3K4me3 signal in Trim28+/D9 mice compared to control.
source: We identified 69 loci that had novel H3K4me3 signal in the Trim28+/D9 mice compared to control (Materials and methods; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on H3K4me3 ChIP-seq data from Trim28 haploinsufficient mice.

claim: The majority of loci with novel H3K4me3 recruitment in Trim28+/D9 mice were evolutionarily recent TEs.
source: The majority of these loci with novel H3K4me3 recruitment were evolutionarily recent TEs (Figure 6B and - supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of H3K4me3 ChIP-seq data from Trim28 haploinsufficient mice.

claim: Loci with novel H3K4me3 in Trim28+/D9 mice had an increase in CFP1 signal relative to control mice.
source: These loci also had an increase in CFP1 signal in Trim28+/D9 mice relative to control mice (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on CFP1 CUT&RUN data from Trim28 haploinsufficient mice.

claim: TEs with a significant increase in gene expression in Trim28+/D9 mice have significantly higher CpG density than non-responsive TE subfamilies.
source: We identified that TEs which have a significant increase in gene expression in the Trim28+/D9 mice compared to wild-type mice have significantly higher CpG density than expected when compared to non-responsive TE subfamilies (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq analysis of Trim28 haploinsufficient mice.

claim: Trim28 haploinsufficiency has previously been shown to impact the Agouti viable yellow mouse coat color.
source: Trim28 haploinsufficiency has previously been shown to impact the Agouti viable yellow mouse coat color (Daxinger et al., 2016) and drive a bimodal obesity phenotype in FVB/NJ mice (Dalgaard et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Trim28 haploinsufficiency drives a bimodal obesity phenotype in FVB/NJ mice.
source: Trim28 haploinsufficiency has previously been shown to impact the Agouti viable yellow mouse coat color (Daxinger et al., 2016) and drive a bimodal obesity phenotype in FVB/NJ mice (Dalgaard et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: VM-IAPs have unique sequence variants that allow them to have diminished KZFP recruitment.
source: We observed that VM-IAPs have unique sequence variants that allow them to have diminished KZFP recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the sequence analysis and ChIP-seq data.

claim: IAPs with the same sequence variants as VM-IAPs are more likely to be polymorphic between individual mouse strains.
source: We also found that IAPs with the same sequence variants as the VM-IAPs are more likely to be polymorphic between individual mouse strains.
evidence: This is based on analysis of structural variants between mouse strains.

claim: The IAPLTRs flanking the 'master' IAP proposed to be responsible for an expansion of IAPs in C3H/HeJ mice has the same sequence as the clade 3 IAPLTR1s.
source: Interestingly, we find that the IAPLTRs flanking the 'master' IAP that has been proposed to be responsible for an expansion of IAPs in C3H/HeJ mice (Rebollo et al., 2020) has the same sequence as the clade 3 IAPLTR1s (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison with the master IAP.

claim: VM-IAPs may be more active in certain mouse strains and may be propagating due to a lack of repression.
source: Together this implies that these VM-IAPs may be more active in certain mouse strains and may be propagating due to a lack of repression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the polymorphism and sequence data.

claim: VM-IAPs have recruitment of ZF-CxxC proteins.
source: We observed that VM-IAPs have recruitment of ZF-CxxC proteins.
evidence: This is based on CFP1 and TET1 binding data.

claim: Deamination of methylated loci could be one means for driving permanent silencing of TEs over time.
source: As TEs can lose CpG density over time, the observation that the CpG rich TEs have the potential for reactivation supports the idea that deamination of methylated loci could be one means for driving permanent silencing of TEs over time (Long et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data and supported by a citation.

claim: VM-IAP loci are established as a result of partial KZFP mediated silencing at CpG dense TEs, which can then be protected from silencing through recruitment of ZF-CxxC containing proteins such as TET1.
source: Based on our results, we propose a model that VM-IAP loci are established as a result of partial KZFP mediated silencing at CpG dense TEs, which can then be protected from silencing through recruitment of ZF-CxxC containing proteins such as TET1 (Figure 6).
evidence: This is the proposed model based on all the experimental findings.
